status: authored 2026-10-02, not yet applied to any world
built_by: tools/frostpeak_camp.py build -> build/datapacks/cobblers_frostpeak_camp; audited by tools/frostpeak_camp_audit.py
owner_request: "i feel like a research site around 2079 115 1048 could be cool. i assume we will have a legendary at teh top of the mountain or close by they are looking into. it would be frostpeak shrine yeah." Then: "i got my x or y wrong, the research site is meant to be at the foot of the south end of the frostpeak". The site (688, 688) was measured and accepted on 2026-10-01.
purpose: A small field camp at Frostpeak's south foot whose researchers study Articuno. Its job in the world: the adopted Articuno shrine (data/adopted_legendary_sites.json adopted_articuno_shrine) has no finder, so the camp is how a player learns where to look - a telescope trained on the east shoulder, field notes on a board, and researchers who point. Nothing here promises the shrine's altar works (adopted_legendary_sites.json a_dead_altar_must_not_block; EXP-048): the researchers observe and speculate, and no step, reward or gate requires the altar.
ground_rule: Every Y is computed by tools/frostpeak_camp.py from tools/ground.py (the canonical heightmap, rounded). Nothing in this file is a Y. Each piece is seated on max(ground under its footprint) + 1, with a foundation down to the ground under any lower column (tools/shrines.py's convention).

site.measured: 2026-10-02 from tools/ground.py: ground y108..113 over x688..727 z688..727, median 111 rounded (raw median 110.62, relief 4.93); the north edge is the high side (y113), the south-east the low (y109). Nothing any built pack writes and no data point lies within 64 blocks (scanned 2026-10-02 against the full checkout's build/datapacks).

shrine.source: data/adopted_legendary_sites.json sites[id=adopted_articuno_shrine]: placement.centre (x, z) and placement.top_y
shrine.aim: the middle of the part of the tower's centre column visible over the shoulder from the telescope, computed from the heightmap

summit.source: data/towns.json towns[id=frostpeak_shrine].centre: the centre of the pressed summit platform (data/sculpt.json pads frostpeak_shrine, radius 55, y310)
summit.aim: the crest that hides it: the highest elevation angle along the summit's bearing, computed from the heightmap. The summit platform itself is not visible from the camp.

blocks.rule: vanilla 1.21.1 only, none a spawn condition in data/spawn_blocks.json (white and red wool are not; grey, light grey, orange and the other coloured wools are). No chests: tools/portals_audit.py records a chest as a Gimmighoul spawn condition, though data/spawn_blocks.json does not list it, so barrels carry the stores. No beds: a bed sets a respawn point, which the blackout recovery owns (docs/mechanics/BLACKOUT_RECOVERY_COUPLING.md).
blocks.display_note: the instrument tubes are block_display entities (the format tools/rift_skin.py already uses), not blocks: a block cannot point at an arbitrary bearing. An entity is erased by an export like an NPC, so the instruments function re-summons them.

pieces.why: a plank deck on the high north edge of the bench, the camp's best view of the mountain
the survey's telescope, trained on the Articuno tower on the east shoulder
the surveyor's theodolite, laid on the summit's bearing and stopped at the false crest that hides it
the field notes, on the deck's south edge where a player walking up from the camp reads them first
the mess: a long tent with a smoker, stores and a counter, its door to the fire
sleeping tent, door towards the fire; bedrolls, not beds
the camp's fire between the tents, with log benches; its smoke is the camp's mark from the slopes
crates and barrels hauled up from the coast
a mast with a lantern and a cauldron for a snow gauge (a cauldron fills with powder snow in a cold biome)

researchers.name: Dr. Signe Halvard
researchers.greeting: Mind the tripod. We are the Frostpeak survey: three of us, one telescope, and a tower on the east shoulder that nobody alive remembers being built.

topics.says: That tower. It stands at bearing {shrine_bearing}, a little east of north, about {shrine_range} blocks off and far above us. Look where the telescope points: its crown shows over the shoulder.
Three winters of notes. Frost on the tower when the slopes are bare, a cold wind out of a clear sky, a pale blue shape the herders swear to. I have not seen it myself. I would very much like to.
There is an old altar in it. Some say it calls the bird; some say it never did. We have not made it do anything, and I would not promise you that anyone can. We watch, and we write down what we see.
North-east, and keep climbing. The shoulder rises about {climb} blocks above this camp and then runs level; the tower stands alone on the snow. Once you are on top you cannot miss it.

researchers.name: Edda Krell
researchers.greeting: The summit? Not from here. That edge up there is a false crest. The middle of the summit table is another {summit_beyond} blocks behind it, flat as a floor.

topics.says: A theodolite. Two sightings on the board: the crest, bearing {summit_bearing}, and the east tower, bearing {shrine_bearing}. Two bearings from two camps give you a position. We have one camp, so we walk.
The mountain is. The wild Pokemon on these slopes are not the lowlands' kind, and the weather turns in an hour. Go up with a team you trust and come back down before dark.

researchers.name: Bram Ostrow
researchers.greeting: Close the flap, you are letting the warm out. The soup is for the survey, but sit a minute.

topics.ask: What do you think is up there?
topics.says: The Doctor says a bird. Edda says a surveying problem. I say nobody hauls stone up a mountain for nothing. Whether anything up there still listens, none of us knows.
Frost on the inside of the tent in summer. Snorunt in the supply crates. And once a shadow crossing the shoulder with no cloud to throw it. Make of that what you like.

spawns.why: Frostpeak already carries 21 surface entries in data/spawns.json (scope frostpeak, level 25-45: Delibird, Crabrawler, Sneasel, Snorunt, Absol, Drampa and their lines; docs/story/ENCOUNTERS.md), which cover the bench. A camp-specific table would add a second author for the same ground for no new species.
